Yes, well, just let me say that I am very disappointed by the amount of false information that's being pushed by the left, especially as it relates to those with pre-existing conditions. They are scaring a lot of people, and I hear that fear pretty regularly this, and I want people to know that the American Health Care Act guarantees coverage to everyone with a pre-existing condition. This has been a priority of mine. And under our plan, insurance companies are prohibited from denying coverage on the basis of a pre-existing condition. They're banned from resending coverage based on a pre-existing condition. And they're prevented from raising premiums on individuals with pre-existing conditions who maintain continuous coverage. Sure. Yeah. So this was an amendment that was passed. It's known as the MacArthur Amendment that was included in the final negotiations and it does allow states to seek a waiver. States right now can seek Medicaid waivers, for example, that allow them more flexibility as they're setting up their Medicaid programs and have proven to be important in giving the states the flexibility to best utilize dollars so that they're spent most effectively to get the best outcomes possible for for people that are on Medicaid. So yes, it includes a provision that would allow state to seek a waiver. I would emphasize that even in this waiver option, no state is able to seek a waiver for the guaranteed issue of coverage, the guaranteed renewability of that coverage, or the prohibition on denying coverage due to a preexisting condition. In addition to that, I joined Fred Optin and some other members of Congress in co-sponsoring an amendment that dedicate $8 billion to reduce premiums or other out-of-pocket expenses for patients in the individual market with pre-existing conditions.
